BLOCKER: `audit_append_late`, `audit_mark_archived`, `audit_drop_partition`, `audit_approve_purge`, `audit_mark_purged` are all `SECURITY DEFINER` with default PUBLIC EXECUTE — any role (including `pf_app`) can insert arbitrary audit events, record fake archives, approve purges, or drop partitions, destroying audit integrity and causing data loss.
MAJOR: `ObjectStore()` in `objectstore.go` panics instead of returning an error when `PF_OBJECT_ROOT` is unset — a library function must not panic.

`audit_provision` trigger checks only `to_regclass('public.' || v_name)` (canonical name); when the grace partition (`audit_grace_YYYYMM`) already covers the target range, the `CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF` fails with 23P01 which is not caught, so inserts into the grace month fail permanently.
`MetricHoldAfterPurge` is incremented when purge is refused due to an active hold, not when a hold is recorded against a purged month — the spoliation metric fires on the wrong event.

`AuditStore.Append` retries only once after `audit_ensure_partitions`; if a concurrent retention drop (AURE namespace) lands between the ensure and the retry, the event is lost — the AC guarantees "no event is lost" but AUDP and AURE locks do not serialize.
`audit_append_late` does not check for active holds on the target month; a late insert into a held month is never captured by the hold archive, violating hold completeness before a partition drop.
MINOR: `audit_partition_config.updated_at` has no ON UPDATE trigger; it shows creation time, not last modification time.
`RestoreMonth` never drops the scratch table; lifecycle is undocumented and operators must clean up manually.
`audit_legal_hold_archive` has no index on `source_partition`; `VerifyHoldExtraction` full-scans on every call.
`Down` records its audit event after commit; a crash between commit and event write loses the permanent record of the down migration.

SQL primitives (`audit_mark_archived`, `audit_approve_purge`, `audit_mark_purged`, `audit_hold_extract`) write no audit event when called directly (bypassing Go), leaving a gap in the "all actions write audit events" guarantee.
`CheckSSE` rejects bare `aws:kms` while `DefaultSSE` returns it when `PF_S3_BUCKET` is set without `PF_S3_KMS_KEY` — the tool is unusable with S3 unless KMS is explicitly configured.
`VerifyHoldExtraction` uses `string_agg` over all held rows; for large hold archives this can exhaust memory or exceed `work_mem`.
`audit_partition_coverage.grace_month` is derived from `min(audit_YYYYMM) - 1 month`, not from the actual `audit_grace_YYYYMM` partition; the value diverges once hot partitions are dropped.
`hashtext`-based advisory lock keys are not guaranteed stable across PostgreSQL major versions; the constant-match test verifies string presence only, not hash equality.
`audit_restore_lock` name implies it takes a lock but it only writes an event; the actual lock is held by the CLI's AURE advisory lock.
`audit_partition_config` `updated_at` is never auto-refreshed when config values change (e.g., `purge_grace_days` update in tests).
`s3store.Put` with `size < 0` leaves `Checksum` empty; `backup()` doesn't verify integrity of the uploaded dump.
NIT: `monthBounds` and `quoteDate` in `archive.go` are dead code in production paths (only exercised by unit tests).
`mustJSON` silently swallows `json.Marshal` errors, returning an empty string.
`audit_provision` catches `unique_violation` (23505) which cannot occur during `CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION OF` — only `duplicate_table` (42P07) is reachable.
`age` exit code is not checked explicitly in `backup()`; the error surfaces indirectly through the pipe error on `obj.Put`.
`PGPASSWORD` is passed via the process environment, readable in `/proc/<pid>/environ` on Linux — consider a `.pgpass` file or socket auth for defense in depth.
